title: Content Strategy for Product UX
editorial_note: Opening revised to lead with the lesson itself. Remaining dialogue is an automated editorial draft; review spoken wording and meaning before final publication.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Content Strategy for Product UX.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Content strategy defines a content product’s purpose, audience, intent, ownership, lifecycle, relationships, and success criteria. In product UX, this applies to labels, instructions, system messages, help, notifications, transactional messages, and service handoffs—not just marketing pages.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Why does that happen?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Start with the user’s task and moment of need. Decide what the content must help someone understand, decide, do, or recover from; where it belongs; what information it depends on; who maintains it; and how it will be evaluated. Content without an owner or review trigger becomes a hidden source of product debt.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Connect content decisions to product behaviour
turns.text: What changes when we look at connect content decisions to product behaviour?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Content strategy defines what information and language a product needs, why it exists, how it is structured, who produces and approves it, where it appears, and how it changes. It joins user need, business or service intent, content design, operations, and governance. A voice guide without a production model is branding; a collection of strings without purpose is inventory.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The strategy identifies content debt as product risk. Clinic access details have no reliable freshness owner; notification text is duplicated in three systems; support scripts use different state names; preparation PDFs cannot adapt after rescheduling. Priorities are based on consequence and reuse, not which page is most visible.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Some problems require new structured data or operational ownership before words can improve.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Success includes comprehension, correct next action, recovery, reduced contradiction, localisation quality, accessibility, and maintenance health. lesson 138 now turns the strategy into sentence-level interaction through plain language.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: tax filing?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A tax product needs more than friendly copy. It needs authoritative rule sources, explanations at decision points, reusable definitions, jurisdiction and effective dates, review workflow, and a plan for annual change. Content strategy makes those dependencies explicit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at build the content system?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Content strategy connects user need, organisational purpose, message, structure, production, governance, and lifecycle. Inventory content and decisions across journeys. Identify source of truth, audience, owner, format, channel, metadata, dependencies, risk, and review date. Remove duplication that creates contradictory states.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Create a model of reusable content types and relationships rather than writing pages independently. Define terminology, hierarchy, voice, accessibility, localisation, legal and policy review, and what changes across context. A status message may appear in product, email, support, and operations; shared meaning matters more than identical copy.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Prioritise high-consequence and high-change content. Establish creation, review, approval, publishing, measurement, correction, and retirement. Measure whether people understand and act successfully, plus search failure, support demand, outdated content, and maintenance effort.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Strategy is realised through operations. A style guide without ownership, tooling, and change paths cannot keep the experience coherent.

turns.speaker: host
turns.act: Create a content strategy decision map
turns.text: What changes when we look at create a content strategy decision map?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Prioritisation combines customer consequence, reach, contradiction, maintenance risk, accessibility, and dependency. A frequently viewed welcome message may matter less than an outdated preparation instruction or a status with no accountable owner.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Some content debt cannot be fixed by writing: missing event semantics, unavailable data, and unresolved policy become product or service work.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: The roadmap includes governance and retirement. Each content type has request, creation, specialist review, localisation, implementation, measurement, update, and archive. Success measures include correct interpretation and action, contradiction rate, freshness, reuse, support demand, and change lead time. Publishing volume is an operating metric, not a customer outcome.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What changes when we look at transfer example: lending?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A loan product needs a governed explanation system for eligibility, rate, repayment, evidence, and adverse decisions. A friendlier landing page cannot compensate for inconsistent calculations and support scripts. Content strategy connects the promise, data, decision, regulation, and lifecycle.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Where does the harder design decision appear?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Treat every message as part of a system. A clever onboarding sentence that contradicts support content or a billing email can damage trust more than a bland but consistent one.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should we look at more closely?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Treat content as a product system with audience, purpose, source of truth, lifecycle, governance, and success criteria. Map which content enables each task, who owns its accuracy, how it changes, and where it appears across channels.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A strong strategy connects customer language and decisions to the underlying model, rather than treating words as a final layer of interface polish.

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Failure modes to watch

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Copy-last workflow: content is added after structure and interaction have already constrained its meaning. Source-of-truth gap: competing channels offer different policy, status, or next steps. Unowned lifecycle: time-sensitive content remains after its validity expires. Template overreach: reusable copy hides material contextual differences.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Can we see that in a concrete product situation?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: A product team adds an onboarding tooltip, an empty state, a help article, and a reminder email. Each is reasonable alone. Together they repeat, contradict, and leave no one responsible for keeping the guidance current.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How does this connect to what we have already learned?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: M07 made the information system coherent. M08 focuses on content as active interface behaviour. lesson 138 makes that behaviour clearer through plain language.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What should I notice the next time I use a product?

turns.speaker: guide
turns.text: Pick one product message. State its audience, task moment, intended action, owner, review trigger, and one signal that would show it is failing.
